item: Three speeds at the same time
content: Usual layers: (1) kick and snare far apart on the slow pulse; (2) a very fast even grid of tuplets; (3) slow melody notes. A live review says that Threshold is fast and slow at the same time.
parameters: At 58 BPM (computed): one beat each 1.03 s; grid 10.6 notes per second; melody in quarter notes and longer
where: Against the Fall of Night; Threshold

content: The bass uses the low B string for sub weight. In Skrontch the very low notes are loud and work like a djent riff on funk bass. Octave pedals add a sub octave below the bass.
parameters: Lowest string: low B. Sub octave from the pedals: 1 octave down
where: Skrontch; Against the Fall of Night (title track)

content: Sax and bass lead above a synth background. Listeners write of 'throbbing bass and glittering synths' and of synths like vaporwave. Chip sounds give a bright top. Piano and strings make a clear, bright harmony above a rhythm that keeps changing.
parameters: 3 registers named in the reviews: low bass, synth middle, bright top (chip sound or piano)
where: Oeteldonk; Perihelion (2021); Clock of the Long Now

item: Drum set as a melodic layer
content: The hi-hat is played open-handed with tom notes at the same time. Off-beat hi-hat 'barks' mark the chorus. The floor tom is used much more than the rack tom. A steady cymbal pattern runs against the groove.
parameters: Hi-hat barks on off-beats in the chorus. Floor tom in place of rack tom

content: Neely: the old resonant double bass drum sound took the low end from the bass player. The bright, clicking kick sound of metal lets fast kick patterns fit in a band.
parameters: Kick with a short, bright attack; the low sustain stays with the bass

content: At a typical moment about 70% of the band plays. At some moments only about 12% plays. League: the band is good at knowing "when to not play".
parameters: With 19 players: about 13 players, and about 2 players (derived)

content: 3 guitarists play the same rhythm and the same chord. Each plays one part of one voicing: the low third, the middle third, or the top third. Chord players can also divide a voicing into top notes and bottom notes.
parameters: 1 voicing; 3 registers; 1 player in each register

content: A rhythm guitarist is part of the percussion section and must blend in. A line is divided into call and response: 1 guitarist plays the two parts; 2 guitarists take one part each. With more players a guitarist plays 2 notes in a bar and not 8. A guitarist makes a delay effect to mark a transition.
parameters: Notes in a bar: 8 for 1 guitarist; 2 for 1 of 3 guitarists

item: Layers that enter one at a time
content: Lingus starts with one keyboard motif. Then drums, bass, percussion, and horns enter, one at a time. A teaching page gives the method: write a 4-bar bass groove, add drums, repeat, then add a 2-bar horn stab pattern off the beat.
parameters: 5 layers; a cyclic chord progression under all layers

content: League on his productions: "a lot of different elements playing very simple parts". League and Bill Laurance use space and simple writing; the depth is in the arrangement.
parameters: Each part is simple; the density comes from the number of parts

item: The bass line doubled by other instruments
content: Cliroy: the bass clarinet doubles the Moog bass line. Waves Upon Waves: trombones and tubas double the bass line. League in a different project: one acoustic guitar doubles the bass line for warmth in the middle register, and an ngoni doubles a guitar figure 1 octave higher.
parameters: Doubling at the unison or 1 octave higher

item: Strings and orchestra with the band
content: Sylva: modal string lines (Sintra); New Orleans brass grooves (Atchafalaya); very large block chords (Gretel); one big theme at the end (The Clearing). Somni: strings under a marimba pattern that repeats; motifs that move through the orchestra; one direction to an arranger was harmony in 5 parts in the style of Gil Evans.
parameters: League wrote the Somni parts so that the band can play them with no orchestra

content: The official songbooks give each tune as a melody part, a guitar part, a keyboard part, and a bass part, with chords and a score.
parameters: Melody parts in C, B-flat, and E-flat. About 50 songbook titles in the store of the band

content: The band tracks stand beside tracks for strings, brass and choir.
parameters: Title track: strings and brass only, no drums. "Crash the Car": band + full choir, strings, brass, flutes. The live version of an electro-pop track adds funk and jazz feel

item: Two players as a full band
content: Keys give bass, chords and lead. Drums give the rest.
parameters: The two instruments stand as close as possible on stage. The album adds 1 harp, 1 violin or viola, 1 cello, 1 flute, 1 contrabass

content: With three drum voices: one very high, one very low, one in the middle.
parameters: Hi-hat, bass drum, snare. Then as wide a range as possible. A very big bass drum leaves no room for the bass player

content: Dense layers of live drums, bass, keyboards and electronics. Live and looped sections alternate.
parameters: Bass lines with a textured tone; the electronics add crunch. BUD: dub feel. BLOOM: a shuffle with clap sounds
where: Beat Music! Beat Music! Beat Music!

content: About 10 strong sounds; each one can be heard. Dry, crisp sounds in front of a soft back.
parameters: Sets of about 100 tracks. Found sounds: car door beep ("Lay-by"), cats, ringtones, system sounds, sprinklers, laughter, a baby sneeze. Beats in the manner of jungle

content: Layer 1 is the riff: guitars or piano left hand, bass and kick drum in rhythmic unison. Layer 2 is the plain 4/4 in cymbals and snare. A third layer can mark the bar lines: a slow lead guitar note or the voice.
parameters: Guitars and bass play the riff an octave apart. Third layer in 'Pineal Gland Optics': one lead guitar tone that changes between C# and D every 8 beats. In 'Entertain Me' the right hand plays all sixteenths while left hand, bass and kick play the group starts

item: Bass, percussion and melody from one guitar
content: With no bass player, a thumped low string acts as bass and percussion while the fingers play a melody above it. Arpeggios cross the full range like a harp. A looper adds a third guitar part.
parameters: Songs often start from a looped chord progression with layers added. Thumping in the upper register can outline arpeggios with a percussive attack ('An Infinite Regression')

content: Cold, clean guitar parts with delay set the mood and go on under the heavy riffs. They use few notes and let the delay fill the space.
parameters: The clean parts are 'more than 50% of the sound'. Riffs are a puzzle of short motives that return in changed forms, with noises between them: pick scrapes, pitch-shifter squeals, harmonics. Method: put down a 4/4 drum beat, play until a hook appears, then polish it

content: The piano plays riffs as single lines in octaves in the low register, with almost no two-voice harmony. Under a heavy riff of bass and drums the pianist plays one line in one register.
parameters: 'Entertain Me': almost no chords; lines and a bass line only. A synthesizer plays some melodies. 'Kars 2': muted piano strings that sound like a santur or qanun

content: Dense melodies and riffs through the whole album, with quieter passages that prepare the loud bursts. Keyboards carry themes and thick synthesizer pads.
parameters: Review terms: 'sheer density of the melodies and riffs'; 'thick nostalgic synths, engaging harmony and crushing riffs'

item: Chamber groups inside a big band
content: The full band rarely plays at once. Changes of texture are more important than solo and accompaniment.
parameters: Space chords rise and fall; percussion comes in or stops; horn solos last a moment. Two keyboards at once: piano with Clavioline or electric celeste, one hand each. Bowed bass holds the piece together
where: Heliocentric Worlds Vol. 1; The Magic City

content: The layers enter one by one over a riff.
parameters: Ostinato: bass clarinet, then bass, then congas and flanged drums; Rhodes lines at 1:00; trumpet and trombone at 1:30. Chameleon: synthesizer bass alone at the start; drums enter at bar 5; Clavinet parts and the horn theme come after

content: One player alternates two roles: a lead line on the synthesizer and chords on the Rhodes.
parameters: Right hand: ARP 2600 line (tension, behind the beat). Left hand or both hands: Rhodes chords with bass and drums (release). Mostly in the first half of the solo

content: All five play at high volume most of the time.
parameters: Guitar through a 100-watt Marshall amplifier "in meltdown mode". Synthesizer through a distorted guitar amplifier to cut through an "incredibly busy sound"

item: Synthesizer bass with or in place of the bass guitar
content: A synthesizer plays the bass line. The bass guitar is free for melody.
parameters: Birdland: synthesizer riff an octave below the bass guitar. Mr. Gone: Oberheim bass for most of the track; the bass guitar enters late. River People: synthesizer "twang" played together with the bass

content: Many layers with changes of depth and tone colour. Ghostly voices, pulsating percussion, trembling bass, trilled synthesizers. Hospital machines and video game sounds are samples.
parameters: Respirator and monitor sounds in "Galaxy in Janaki"; harp on 8 of 17 tracks

content: Vinyl crackle, rain, pitched vocal pieces, filtered Reese bass, dark pads.
parameters: Tempo 130 to 140 BPM

content: A dense background from rain samples, tape noise and vinyl crackle. The sample is slowed a little to lower its pitch. Chops of about two bars start on the grid and get no correction inside, so the tempo drifts.
parameters: Drums mostly in septuplet swing

content: Few drum hits and a dominant sub. Dub echo, reverb and wide pads fill the space. High-pass filters on most other parts keep room for the sub. Deep dubstep uses claps and rimshots, not large snares, and a layer of cassette noise.
parameters: Pads wide; leads narrow
